{hrs:14, fromTo:'Climb The Tempest', section:'Descent', note:'Alpine start from camp up to the base, then a long day of aid and free climbing on sustained 5.9-5.11/A2 terrain before rappelling back down to the basin.'}
{n:2, title:'Climb The Tempest', hours:14, objective:'Aid/free climb all 9 pitches and return to camp'}

contradictions.why: The PUBLISHED TIMES section's own 'section' labels are swapped: the 3-hr hike-in day is tagged section:'Climb' and the actual 14-hr climbing day is tagged section:'Descent'. contradictions.fact: Best season window

claims.says: Best in a cool, stable freeze — commonly climbed late April-May or Sep-Oct
Best in spring, roughly March through June, as soon as trailhead/road access allows, when the couloir is continuously snow-filled; by mid-to-late summer it can bare out to Class 4 rock.
Early-season snow can be thin/unconsolidated; road access (FR 7601) also closes by fall.

contradictions.why: `season` names two good windows (late Apr–May AND Sep–Oct), but best_season only endorses a March–June window (extending outside season's stated late-Apr/May range) and drops the fall window entirely; climate.fall actively undercuts season's Sep–Oct claim by describing thin snow and a closing road in fall.
contradictions.internal_resolution: best_season and climate.spring/climate.fall together describe this as a spring-only snow climb (Mar–Jun) that is out of condition by fall; season's 'Sep-Oct' alternative window is contradicted by climate.fall's own description of that period.
